items.claim: The hundred-cubit figures are misattributed by verse: the row places a temple / separate-place / building triad "each measured at a hundred cubits" at MT 41:13-14, but on the bytes MT 41:13 gives one hundred cubits to the house and a second hundred cubits to the separate place together with the building and its walls as one joint figure, and MT 41:14 gives one hundred cubits to the frontage of the house with the separate place eastward. The building receives a hundred-cubit length of its own only at MT 41:15, outside the cited pair of verses. Everything else the row asserts on the Masoretic layer collates exactly: the five upper dots at MT 41:20 stand on one word and are one of the two puncta sites in the book, the ketiv/qere at MT 41:15 is a form variant and no numeral is in dispute there, the speak-verb at MT 41:22 differs from the say-verb at MT 41:4, and the paseq tally of five occurrences across four verses matches the corpus record.
items.both_sides: Onset: MT 41:12 turns to a newly named measured object and MT 41:13 brings a fresh measuring verb, with no formula and no Masoretic paragraph mark anywhere in MT chs 40-42 to corroborate it. Close: MT 41:26 ends on the side rooms and thresholds, and MT 42:1 opposite carries a two-verb transport out to the outer court. The close side is much the stronger of the two, which is what the row already concedes by holding its confidence at the lowest band; the boundary stands and the confidence band is honest.

suggested_fix.fact: The building has a hundred-cubit length of its own at MT 41:15; within MT 41:13-14 the three hundred-cubit figures are the house, the separate place taken together with the building and its walls, and the eastward frontage of the house with the separate place.

items.claim: Two Masoretic facts are wrong. First and materially: the row clears the ketiv/qere at MT 42:16 as a spelling variant that is not a numeral and does not affect the reed count, but the read form there is the plural of the hundred-word, the multiplier itself, against a written form that is the cubit-word. The three parallel perimeter verses MT 42:17, MT 42:18 and MT 42:19 and the summary at MT 42:20 all carry the hundred-word plainly, so the variant at MT 42:16 is exactly a numeral variant and it is the magnitude of that one perimeter figure that turns on it. The quotation the row binds to MT 42:16 for its measure verb also carries no ketiv/qere disclosure alongside it. Second: the row states that each of the four cardinal measurements opens with a measure verb, which holds at MT 42:16 and MT 42:17 but not at MT 42:18, which opens with the object marker and puts the verb after the direction, nor at MT 42:19, which opens with a turning verb and puts the measure verb fourth.
items.both_sides: Onset: MT 42:15 pairs a completion notice with a transport verb, which is a close-grade device pressed into onset service, and the row says so. Close: MT 42:20 ends on the separating purpose of the wall, and MT 43:1 opposite carries a transport verb and opens the glory material. Neither side has any paragraph-mark corroboration, because the book carries no mark between the open section at MT 39:29 and the closed section at MT 43:9. The seam itself is well supported from both sides and stands; what fails is the clearance given to the textual variant inside the row, and a measurement row that reports a numeral variant as not a numeral is the one error a downstream consumer will take as already checked.

suggested_fix.fact: The ketiv/qere at MT 42:16 is a numeral-bearing variant: the read form is the plural hundred-word and the written form is the cubit-word, so the magnitude of the east-side perimeter figure turns on it, and the three parallel verses MT 42:17-42:19 together with the summary at MT 42:20 carry the hundred-word without a variant. The verse also needs its ketiv/qere disclosed alongside the measure-verb quotation, and the clause-initial measure verb holds only at MT 42:16 and MT 42:17.

items.claim: An editorial note the corpus records at MT 43:11 is undisclosed. That verse carries, besides its two ketiv/qere notes, an untyped note recording that the edition has abandoned or added a ketiv/qere at that point relative to the printed critical edition, following the manuscript against it. The row discloses only the two variant notes, so the one disclosure that qualifies the reliability of those very notes is the one left out, and the row is a three-verse unit whose whole warrant is the Masoretic texture of those three verses. The rest of the row is exact: the address form at MT 43:10 lacks the leading conjunction and is correctly held apart from the twenty-three-verse family that carries it; both disputed readings at MT 43:11 are suffix and number variants on the form-word and the law-word and neither is a numeral; the law-of-the-house title does open and close MT 43:12 as a doubled frame; no paragraph mark falls between the closed section at MT 43:9 and the doubled closed section at MT 43:27; and the single paseq in the span is at MT 43:12.

Both edges hold and the three-verse length is warranted by the doubled frame, so the boundary stands and the lowest confidence band is a fair reading of a three-verse unit with no mark of its own.
